nist_800_171_r3.name: NIST SP 800-171 Rev 3 security requirement -> source NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 controls (97 requirements)
nist_800_171_r3.source: NIST CPRT export of SP 800-171 Rev 3: https://csrc.nist.gov/extensions/nudp/services/json/nudp/framework/version/sp_800_171_3_0_0/export/json?element=all (sha256 19d18ef88700e468f273a4bb0a00e76f1dab762f5639e5de75592fda4e61c4fa); the export's external_reference relationships to SP 800-53 Rev 5.1.1 are the requirement's source controls

The STIG -> 800-53 spine is at base-control granularity, so a mapped enhancement never gets a verdict through it and a framework id that maps to one is never 'satisfied' on benchmark results alone

pci_dss_v4.name: pci_dss_v4
pci_dss_v4.source: NO source whose licence allows it. PCI SSC publishes no PCI DSS v4 -> SP 800-53 mapping and its documents are not freely redistributable. NIST's OLIR catalog lists one PCI DSS 4.0.1 -> CSF 2.0 reference (id 183, posted 2025-12-23), submitted by an independent third party, not by PCI SSC or NIST; chaining it through CSF 2.0 to 800-53 would be a derived mapping from a non-authoritative source. Checked 2026-11-24.

An id map extracted from it is a derivative and this repository is Apache-2.0, so the map is NOT shipped. Build it locally from a workbook you download: python3 scripts/gen_nist_framework_maps.py --cis-file <workbook.xlsx> --out <dir outside the repository>/data.json. Checked 2026-11-24.
